hereHead: You are here: 0.1.2 is published (v0.1.2 on 233da8f, 2026-09-19). Main carries unpushed work for 0.1.3: the reconnect hold (mirrors, bases and the partner mirror survive a link drop), the 30-minute cap on the reconnect wait, a quiet post-leave socket reset, the marker day fix, the player docs on the minimized-window stall, and the launcher's Agent bridge checkbox. Left before V1 sign-off: Phase 23's forum-thread URL and the COOP TEST Ziggurat start, then what remains of the Phase 19 checklist under ATTENTION.
here: 0.1.2 is published. Tag v0.1.2 on 233da8f, coop-0.1.2.zip attached at releases/tag/v0.1.2 (2026-09-19). Unpushed on main, for 0.1.3: a link drop inside the reconnect window no longer tears down the guest's mirrors, bases or the partner mirror; Wait 5 more minutes stops at 30 minutes remaining; the socket reset after a clean partner leave is one info line; the marker day is a calendar count; the player docs describe the minimized-window stall; the launcher gets an Agent bridge checkbox with role default ports. 0.1.3 is cut when the user says so. Everything below is outstanding. Phase 23: put the forum-thread URL in docs/player/LISTING.md and modThreadId in coop.version (still 0), and remove or dev-gate the COOP TEST Ziggurat start (coopZigguratStart/coopZigguratPicked in data/campaign/rules.csv). Then Phase 19: the two-instance checklist steps listed under ATTENTION, with fixes limited to what fails.

attention.head: Phase 23: forum-thread URL and the COOP TEST Ziggurat start
attention.state: open; two edits, neither is code
attention.body: (1) Create the forum thread, then put its URL in docs/player/LISTING.md and its numeric id in modThreadId in coop.version (0 today, so Version Checker offers no link). Verify: Version Checker's mod entry links to the thread. (2) Remove or dev-gate the COOP TEST start: rows coopZigguratStart and coopZigguratPicked in data/campaign/rules.csv (option 6, a Ziggurat plus 1,000,000 credits). Verify: a new game shows five occupation choices, or six only with the dev flag. The forced tutorial skip and forced Normal difficulty stay; they are permanent mod behaviour (see the plan, Phase 23).

attention.head: Phase 31 launcher: one pass on the published build, plus three rows never exercised
attention.body: Run the launcher path once on the published build: fix button on both red install rows, Check my connection, Coop published the settings-file in both logs, no getSaveDirName WARN, save finder shows the new campaign. Then three rows that have never been in front of a game: the wrong-save notice (smoke step 13): send an invite that carries a campaign pick, have the guest load a different save, expect the notice naming the right save before the seed lock refuses; stale forks jar: an old coop-forks.jar beside a fresh coop.jar must turn the forks row red; touched game jar: a starfarer_obf.jar with a modified timestamp must leave the Game version row grey, not red.

attention.head: Smoke steps Sessions 1-5 never reached
attention.state: open; each has a pass criterion
attention.body: Step 23, guest storage unlock at a hidden pirate base right after a reconnect blip: pass = the unlock lands on both engines and the host log has no flagged unknown market. Step 33, guest saturation bombardment decivilising the host's colony: pass = the next reconnect passes the fingerprint check. S4-B, mothballed hull cargo: find a trade fleet carrying hulls; pass = the guest draws them mothballed, not as 0% CR warships. Ambient-spawn nudge: park the guest alone in a populated system until a DisposableFleetManager spawn appears; pass = it appears outside sensor range plus 500 (log line from the forked setLocationAndOrders). Large locker: 30 or more refitted hulls in one storage; pass = at most Coop MARKET_SNAPSHOT is large, never refused. Post-battle mirror freeze expiry needs a lost BATTLE_RESULT and has no cheap trigger; stays unit-verified. UPnP router without GetSpecificPortMappingEntry: cannot be exercised on this network (the MikroTik answers it); expected behaviour is a conflict report and a port change, not an eviction.

attention.head: Phase 12c manual residue: hire an officer with the partner on the same market
attention.body: At a market with officers in its comm directory, with the partner docked at the same market: the host hires one, the guest reopens the directory. Pass = the officer is gone on the guest with no duplicate. Then the feel pass from Phase 12c's manual list.

attention.head: S4-C: fleet churn in far systems still resends the NPC set
attention.body: Structural NPC_FLEET_SET sends are scoped to the two observers' locations, but route fleets despawning in the host's own system count as near, so a parked pair still sees about one 20 KB set every 7 s. Candidate fix: treat the despawn of a fleet the guest has never mirrored as far. Measure: count Coop sent NPC_FLEET_SET lines in the host log over a 130 s window with both fleets parked; target is near zero.

attention.head: Hyperspace storms hit one player and the other never sees why
attention.state: documented; Phase 26 M4 would replicate it, not built
attention.body: Storm cells are rolled per engine, so a strike on the guest (CR loss, repair-tracker event hyperstorm) is invisible on the host and reads as an unexplained CR drop. Not a bug in V1; stated in docs/player/LIMITATIONS.md and the 0.1.1 changelog. The fix is Phase 26 M4 (terrain-plugin subclass, one capture per generation), specced in the plan.

attention.head: Parked Phase 14 fallout (cosmetic)
attention.body: Synthesized customs pursuit of the guest reads coarser than vanilla steering (mechanism and ceiling in starsector-runtime-limitations.md, NPC mirrors); re-judge at the next customs encounter, since Phase 29 M1's kinematic drive landed after the verdict. Also parked: NPC mirrors carry d-mods but not the autofit weapon loadout, and with the two players in different populated systems only one gets ambient spawns (single currSpawnLoc).

attention.head: Six vanilla classes are forked (pinned 0.98a-RC8)
attention.body: The guest-presence family (RouteManager, PlayerVisibleFleetManager, DisposableFleetManager + two subclasses, SourceBasedFleetManager) plus the pre-existing Misc/procgen forks ride the coop-forks.jar classpath shadow. A Starsector update requires re-extracting each file and re-applying the small additive diffs; the shared runtime guard (CoopPresenceRegistry.getForFork) loudly disables the presence terms on a version mismatch instead of drifting silently. Re-fork procedure: starsector-runtime-limitations.md, Classpath forks.

phases.summary: Replicates slipstreams as outcome polylines, abyssal temporary systems via keyed EPEC re-execution, and (M4, open) hyperspace storm grids as per-generation captures so both players share hyperspace ambient content.

document residual divergences + retire v1 accept-divergence entries
commit
phases.note: Requires Phase 13 (suppressor + coop-forks.jar); builds on Phase 9 NPC mirrors + Phase 8 hyper position. Review pass 2026-09-05 corrected four points against the API source: slipstream fades scale travel intensity (despawn fades run up to 27 days), so fade state is replicated instead of drawn locally; the dire-hints draw is filtered by per-install UniqueEncounterData, so the host ships its resolved choice; entities inside a generated system take Sector.genUID() ids that differ per client, so they are keyed by creation ordinal; and acceptance is gated on bridge diffs, not unit tests. Ordered first post-V1 (after 19, before 33/22) by user decision the same day; scope M1 + M2, M3 and stretch open. M4 (storms) added the same evening after a source read: the automaton's committed grid only changes at the 1.5-2.5 day interval and has a deflate codec already, trackers are local-player-centric (±10000 su) and get keyed durations instead of being shipped, and the plugin is replaceable through terrain.json so no classpath fork is needed. Open like M3; independent of M1-M3.

phases.title: Campaign Motion Smoothness
phases.summary: Pulled into V1 2026-08-20: root cause verified live (speed-clamped chase + arrival dead zone in the mirror drive path = ~1 Hz teleports; orbit pair = worst case). M1 mirror interpolation slots after 18; M2 adaptive cadence needs 20. No player-facing rate knob ever.
residue: M2 BUILT 2026-09-03 (5f01a98, 1851 green): CoopCadenceController (host-decided per link, p50 RTT / 10 s loss / queue backlog / fallback; down at loss>=10% or p50>=400 ms or backlog or fallback, up after 30 s clean at loss<=3% and p50<300 ms), LINK_STATUS.cadenceHz pulled forward on change, guest follows, fallback = FLOOR pin (one mechanism, FALLBACK_STREAM_INTERVAL deleted), adaptive interp delay from FLEET_SNAPSHOT arrival jitter (200 ms clean default, 400 ms floor, clamp 150-500, 5 s hold), redundancy depth 2 on lossy floor with the chunk budget widened, HUD/intel/feed surfacing; TOP 20 Hz defined but dark

M2 CERTIFIED 2026-09-03 on the six-profile shaped matrix (m1 clean hold never left 10 Hz; m2 loss 12% down at +14 s / up 35 s after; m3 RTT 460 ms down at +53 s; m4 UDP block = same-millisecond fallback + floor pin, depth 1 on TCP; m5 three bursts = one down one up; m6 jitter: delay 236-243 ms then back to 211-217, guest speed-probe tail 2/22 > 1.15, max 1.215 = baseline max); finding M2-F1 (ceil in the delay formula gave 300 ms on a clean link) fixed in 025c374 (delay = 2*interval + sigma, 25 ms step); observation M2-O1: RTT-driven transitions trail the event by 50-80 s (p50 over 96 s of PING history)

inputs from the 2026-09-02 WAN smoke: speed-probe tail above 1.15 under RTT jitter (53/181 ms) is M2's acceptance signal for the adaptive interp delay; RTT samples carry a frame interval per side, so key the tier on p50 with hysteresis, not p95
phases.note: M1 BUILT + clean-link smoke verified 2026-08-24 (partner-mirror inclusion settled: included); game-time send cadence under FF landed with 7b 2026-09-02. M2 built + certified 2026-09-03; the shaped-loopback pass doubled as M1's pending loss/reorder QA (m2/m6). M2 needed Phase 20's CoopLinkQuality/LINK_STATUS, which landed 2026-09-02, so M2 was unblocked and next in the order.

phases.title: Agent Bridge + Starsector MCP
phases.summary: Dev tooling: a dormant localhost TCP bridge in each game instance plus an external MCP server, letting the agent query and diff live game state and run setup verbs — automates 7 of the 12c smoke's 10 checks and pays off again at Phase 19.
phases.note: Built, live-verified, AND polished 2026-08-25, same day as the spec (c51ee37/4ed9a77 build; live check + automated 7-item 12c smoke portion all PASS; 1f4aed2 fixed every run-surfaced nit and added status.pause stall diagnosis, markets verb, diffable visibility.view, ss_diff ignore, help-popup seeding; 959 mod + 31 MCP tests). Read + diff + setup verbs only — no UI synthesis; UI-listener checks (claim race, sell-back, hire) stay manual by design. Phase 23 dormancy checklist line added.

phases.title: Coop Launcher
phases.summary: A Windows launcher window (Swing jar on the game's bundled JRE) that writes the options file the mod already reads, checks the install and fixes the two rows it can (vmparams classpath, enabled_mods) with a Fix button, runs the host doctor and a launcher-to-launcher test connection, names which save each player should load for the picked campaign, then starts the game with a log tail. The invite carries address, port, seed, password, world settings and the campaign id, so the guest pastes one line.
introduces: install check rows + a Fix button on vmparams and enabled_mods
campaign picker + "load this save" hint from coop_saves.json.data
residue: two-instance smoke deferred into Phase 19 (now also the Fix button, the save-finder hint, the in-game wrong-save notice and getSaveDirName handle resolution)
Windows only; starsector.sh installs keep the manual path
seed over the wire stays a Maybe
no external reachability probe
phases.note: Created, decided AND built 2026-09-03 (2275 -> 2445 tests, five commits b1372f7..5cc5303): launcher core, dark FlatLaf redesign, bug-report zip, update check, default password, every -Dcoop flag in Advanced, invite with world settings, launch gate, COOP-GAME game-version check, package-release.ps1, Version Checker file, docs rewrite, README, issue forms. Two more landed 2026-09-04. The Fix button (8c22624, 3a85328) moved the two install edits from report-only into scope: the launcher writes the coop-forks.jar classpath entry into vmparams (backup first, ISO-8859-1, one line) and adds coop to enabled_mods.json, and offers an elevated relaunch when Windows refuses the write under Program Files. The save finder (2faeb2b mod side, f43b63f launcher side, 2678 -> 2722 tests) closes the "which of my saves is this invite for" gap: the mod indexes every save by campaign id into saves/common/coop_saves.json.data, the launcher joins that index to the folders on disk, the host picks the campaign from a drop-down, the invite carries the id as cid, both cards say which save to load, and coop.expectedCampaignId lets the mod repeat the answer in-game when the wrong save is loaded anyway. Two-instance smoke still DEFERRED into Phase 19 (user, 2026-09-03), and it now has to cover both.

phases.title: Shared Submarkets + Storage
phases.summary: Host-canonical storage, black market and military submarket on the same snapshot-on-open plus guest-delta path the open market uses. Shared storage at every market is how the two players park and exchange ships; ship listings gained weapon groups, hull damage, display name and module loadouts so a refitted ship survives the round trip. Hidden-base markets are paired across the two engines, and credits move between players from the Coop Options page.

phases.note: Specced and BUILT 2026-09-05, the same day, on user decisions taken that morning (all storage markets, black + military included, no migration). Six feature commits c5e3060..2fdbf24 plus four red-team fix commits, merged at 6ba4bca; additions A (hidden-base markets) and B (credit transfer) both in scope. A five-lens red-team pass the same day (credits, ship-detail codec, market/storage integrity, unlock/commission/ids, lifecycle) found five P0s, all fixed: a grant marked applied before the wallet write, a capture failure deleting the guest's stored ship, a deposit at an unpaired hidden base destroyed by the next snapshot, a reconnect that never re-baselined unlocks or commission, and cargo destroyed in the post-edge unmapped window. Nothing has been in front of two running games yet.
